meaning:
συν-σταυρόω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ,
to crucify together with: pass., with dative, Jhn.19:32; id. before σύν, Mat.27:44, Mrk.15:32. Metaphorical, of the mystical death of the Christian with Christ: Rom.6:6, Gal.2:20 (Eccl.).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: The robbers also who were crucified with him cast on him the same reproach.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.” Those who were crucified with him also insulted him.
Therefore the soldiers came, and broke the legs of the first, and of the other who was crucified with him;
knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.
